notes: This patch release depends exactly on bifrost.public.packs 0.18.0. Its catalog loads on Bifrost 0.15.3 and later, and it was qualified on released Bifrost 0.15.4. Changed (#494): bifrost.correctness.empty-failure-handler (bifrost.code-smells 4.1.1) no longer reports a catch or except clause that states an intent to ignore the failure: a comment inside the clause, a binding named _, ignore, ignored, expected or tolerated, or a Python clause naming only ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError. A TODO, FIXME or XXX comment keeps the clause reported. Rust and Go failure branches are unchanged. On nine public repositories findings fell from 512 to 104, and precision on a 60-finding production sample rose from 43% to 93%. With packs 0.18.0 the following opt-in policies can now report from the released packs alone: bifrost.security.python.httpx-, aiohttp- and urllib3-tls-verification-disabled on their pinned package versions, python.flask-request-to-parse-qs, python.flask-request-to-decompress (now including zlib and gzip decompression) and javascript.process-input-to-fetch-url. Still unable to report from the released packs alone: python.requests-tls-verification-disabled (its pack is not delivered), javascript.file-content-to-unbounded-decompression (it needs the review-required Node fs packs) and rust.cleartext-logging (its pack is not delivered). All nine stay opt-in. bifrost.security.python.flask-request-to-urlopen and django-request-to-urlopen stay opt-in until a released Bifrost carries bifrost-dev#15505. All other policies, IDs and required capabilities are unchanged from rules 0.18.0. This release does not qualify the full policy set or imply complete analysis.
